issue.title: Rule proposal: prefer `String(x)` over `x.toString()` (consistent conversion to string)
issue.body:
### Description

There are (at least) 3 ways we can convert a value to string: `${x}`, `x.toString()`, `String(x)`. We can get rid of the first one with `'no-implicit-coercion': [1, { disallowTemplateShorthand: true }]`, but the second one remains.

For numbers, we already have https://github.com/sindresorhus/eslint-plugin-unicorn/blob/main/docs/rules/prefer-number-coercion.md. I didn't find a similar rule for strings.

### Examples

```js
// ❌
const str = x.toString();

// ✅
const str = String(x);
```


### Proposed rule name

prefer-string-coercion

### Additional Info

The rule probably should not report `x?.toString()`, because this gives a different result for nullish values.

issue.title: Some `❌` doc examples aren't reported by their rule
issue.body:
### Description

I linted every `❌`/`✅` example in `docs/rules/` with its rule, and 13 `❌` examples in 8 docs aren't reported as written. The rules look fine. Each example is missing something the rule needs, and is reported once that's added.

Five docs use a bare identifier where the rule needs to know the type. These rules only report when the receiver is known to be a `Set`, an array, a string, and so on, from a literal, a constructor, a type annotation, or type information:

- `prefer-set-methods` ([L19](https://github.com/sindresorhus/eslint-plugin-unicorn/blob/e81da0169b5f5b744e5be9c14792bd6de207b22f/docs/rules/prefer-set-methods.md?plain=1#L19), [L27](https://github.com/sindresorhus/eslint-plugin-unicorn/blob/e81da0169b5f5b744e5be9c14792bd6de207b22f/docs/rules/prefer-set-methods.md?plain=1#L27), [L35](https://github.com/sindresorhus/eslint-plugin-unicorn/blob/e81da0169b5f5b744e5be9c14792bd6de207b22f/docs/rules/prefer-set-methods.md?plain=1#L35), [L56](https://github.com/sindresorhus/eslint-plugin-unicorn/blob/e81da0169b5f5b744e5be9c14792bd6de207b22f/docs/rules/prefer-set-methods.md?plain=1#L56)): `set` and `otherSet`. As written, the union example is the same code as the `✅` example `new Set([...iterable, ...otherIterable])` below it, apart from the names. The doc also says the union case is "autofixed only when every spread operand is known to be a `Set`", which reads as if it's still reported otherwise, but nothing is reported unless both operands are known.
- `prefer-array-iterable-methods` ([L23](https://github.com/sindresorhus/eslint-plugin-unicorn/blob/e81da0169b5f5b744e5be9c14792bd6de207b22f/docs/rules/prefer-array-iterable-methods.md?plain=1#L23), [L35](https://github.com/sindresorhus/eslint-plugin-unicorn/blob/e81da0169b5f5b744e5be9c14792bd6de207b22f/docs/rules/prefer-array-iterable-methods.md?plain=1#L35)): `array`
- `prefer-string-starts-ends-with` ([L41](https://github.com/sindresorhus/eslint-plugin-unicorn/blob/e81da0169b5f5b744e5be9c14792bd6de207b22f/docs/rules/prefer-string-starts-ends-with.md?plain=1#L41)): `someString`
- `prefer-abort-signal-any` ([L19](https://github.com/sindresorhus/eslint-plugin-unicorn/blob/e81da0169b5f5b744e5be9c14792bd6de207b22f/docs/rules/prefer-abort-signal-any.md?plain=1#L19)): `signals`. This is the doc's only `❌` example.
- `no-useless-coercion` ([L53](https://github.com/sindresorhus/eslint-plugin-unicorn/blob/e81da0169b5f5b744e5be9c14792bd6de207b22f/docs/rules/no-useless-coercion.md?plain=1#L53)): `array` in `Number(array.length)`

Declaring the receiver in each block would fix these, for example `const set = new Set([1, 2]);`, `const signals = [firstSignal, secondSignal];`, or `declare const someString: string;` in a `ts` block. `prefer-array-iterable-methods` and `prefer-string-starts-ends-with` already say the receiver has to be known, so the examples would match their own text.

The other three:

- `escape-case` ([L49](https://github.com/sindresorhus/eslint-plugin-unicorn/blob/e81da0169b5f5b744e5be9c14792bd6de207b22f/docs/rules/escape-case.md?plain=1#L49), [L99](https://github.com/sindresorhus/eslint-plugin-unicorn/blob/e81da0169b5f5b744e5be9c14792bd6de207b22f/docs/rules/escape-case.md?plain=1#L99)): `'\ca'` and `'\cA'` are strings, where `\c` isn't an escape (`'\ca'` is just `'ca'`). The rule reports `/\ca/`, and `/\cA/` with `'lowercase'`, so these could be regex examples.
- `prefer-dom-node-html-methods` ([L54](https://github.com/sindresorhus/eslint-plugin-unicorn/blob/e81da0169b5f5b744e5be9c14792bd6de207b22f/docs/rules/prefer-dom-node-html-methods.md?plain=1#L54)): `element.innerHTML = userProvidedHTML` is only reported with `checkSetHTML: true`, which is off by default. The intro says assignments aren't checked by default, but the example is listed under "Examples" with no note. `no-instanceof-builtins` handles the same situation with a one-line note ([L76](https://github.com/sindresorhus/eslint-plugin-unicorn/blob/e81da0169b5f5b744e5be9c14792bd6de207b22f/docs/rules/no-instanceof-builtins.md?plain=1#L76)).
- `prefer-temporal` ([L117](https://github.com/sindresorhus/eslint-plugin-unicorn/blob/e81da0169b5f5b744e5be9c14792bd6de207b22f/docs/rules/prefer-temporal.md?plain=1#L117)): the `checkMethods` example has TypeScript syntax (`date: Date`) in a `js` block. It's reported in a `.ts` file with type information, so the block could be `ts`.

### Examples

```js
// ❌ Not reported
const union = new Set([...set, ...otherSet]);
```

```js
// ❌ Reported
const set = new Set([1, 2]);
const otherSet = new Set([2, 3]);
const union = new Set([...set, ...otherSet]);
```

```js
// ❌ Not reported
const foo = '\ca';

// ❌ Reported
const bar = /\ca/;
```

### Additional Info

Checked on `main` at e81da016, along the lines of the last comment on #428. Each example above is not reported as written, and is reported with the change described.

Two of these went stale after a rule change. The `escape-case` `\c` examples date back to the first version (#63), but #294 stopped treating `\c` in strings as an escape and only checks it in regexes; #2559 later added the `'lowercase'` example in the same form. The `prefer-dom-node-html-methods` assignment example predates #3541, which made assignments opt-in with `checkSetHTML`. The others were added with their rule or feature (#3075, #3087, #3283, #3358, #3439, #3447).

I left out examples that only fail because of the environment, like ones that read `package.json` or files on disk (`expiring-todo-comments`, `no-missing-local-resource`, `no-unnecessary-polyfills`), and ones that need type information (`no-non-function-verb-prefix`, `no-useless-override`, and the operator examples in `no-useless-coercion`).

issue.title: Question about yielding the event loop
issue.body:
Hey, I don't know if you have a spot for discussions, apologies if I have overlooked it. 

I'm having a problem with the prometheus client where we want to force tick() to happen at least every <interval> milliseconds while running a list comprehension. Since some of the functions may not be async, and the processing phase certainly isn't, we are going to have to to something explicit to make sure that happens.

My first thought was, "surely Sindre has something for this," but not one that I can find.  Am I wrong? Do you have any suggestions on how to accomplish that?

issue.title: Mark dictation clipboard writes so clipboard managers skip them

labels.name: priority: normal
labels.description: Functional/UX bugs and measured performance fixes after high-impact reliability work.

labels.name: triage: small-fix
labels.description: Bug/perf PR with <100 total added lines, not net LOC; review candidate, not merge approval.

issue.body: ## Problem Dictation pastes by putting the text on the clipboard, pressing ⌘V, and putting the user's previous clipboard back 0.5s later. Clipboard managers record both changes. Each dictation therefore adds two history entries: 1. the dictated text 2. a duplicate of whatever the user had copied before macOS doesn't tell clipboard managers which app wrote to the clipboard, so they credit the app in front. Muesli is a background app, so both entries look like they came from the app the user was dictating into (Brave in the screenshot). Users can't hide them by excluding Muesli in their clipboard manager. This is the complaint from #27. #28 closed that issue with save/restore, which keeps the user's clipboard intact but still leaves entries in clipboard history. **Before** (CopyClip, after one dictation): ## Fix Both writes in `PasteController` now carry the [nspasteboard.org](http://nspasteboard.org) markers that tell clipboard managers not to record an entry: - `org.nspasteboard.TransientType` - `org.nspasteboard.ConcealedType` They go on the dictated text and on the restored clipboard. Clipboard managers differ in which marker they check. A probe against CopyClip showed it skips only `ConcealedType` and records `TransientType`, `AutoGeneratedType` and the older legacy markers. Setting both covers CopyClip and managers that check only `TransientType`. The dictated text is now written as one `NSPasteboardItem` with the string and both markers, so a clipboard manager can never see the text without its markers. Restoring the clipboard is shared with Quill's selection-copy fallback, so that restore is skipped by clipboard managers too. The ⌘C write from the target app itself is still recorded, because that write belongs to the other app. Pasting itself is unchanged: target apps read `.string` as before, and the markers are empty data types. ## Testing - New test: `staged and restored clipboard writes carry clipboard-manager skip markers` - `swift test --filter PasteControllerTests`: 27/27 pass - Manual test on macOS with CopyClip running: dictated into Brave. Neither the dictation nor a duplicate of the earlier clipboard appears in history. ⌘V afterwards still pastes the original clipboard. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. Autofix is disabled. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Temporary text placed on the clipboard during paste is now marked so clipboard managers can skip saving it. The markers are also retained when the previous clipboard contents are restored, helping prevent staged or restored clipboard items from being captured by clipboard managers.

comment.body: FYI, this is needed to preserve compatibility with clipboard apps like [Pure Paste](https://sindresorhus.com/pure-paste).

issue.body:

CI workflow [main](https://github.com/sindresorhus/got/blob/main/.github/workflows/main.yml) tests on `ubuntu-latest`

GitHub Actions is in a [staged deployment process](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-09-17-ubuntu-26-generally-available-and-latest-migration/)

> The ubuntu-latest label will migrate from Ubuntu 24.04 to Ubuntu 26.04. This migration will roll out gradually between October 19 and November 19, 2026. During this window, workflows that use ubuntu-latest will automatically move to Ubuntu 26.04.

issue.title: Clamp cursor-up to the viewport
issue.body:
Takes over #917, which went quiet after the last review.

When a frame is taller than the viewport, the rows above the viewport are in scrollback, and a cursor-up past the top row makes some terminals jump there (the "scroll to top" reports). This clamps every place that moves the cursor up to the viewport:

- `buildCursorSuffix` (the `useCursor` case Sindre pointed out on #917) and the cursor-only path
- `clear()` with and without a cursor, in both renderers
- the standard renderer's rewrite, which now erases only the visible rows
- the incremental renderer, which writes the whole frame instead of diffing when the previous frame's top is above the viewport, since the diff walks up to that top
- the resize erase in `ink.tsx`

Erasing with a cursor now walks up only to the cursor's real row in the viewport (`getCursorViewportRow`), since after a clamped suffix it can already be on the top row. Streams with no rows (or 0) are never clamped.

Tests: the log-update tests follow the cursor row through every write and fail on any cursor-up past the top, and `test/cursor.tsx` covers it through `render()` with `useCursor`. 8 of the new tests fail on master. `npm test` otherwise matches master: the 6 `use-animation` failures on both come from `@sinonjs/fake-timers` 15.5.0 (released Nov 15), and pass again on 15.4.0.

Fixes the case Sindre found on #917 (`\x1b[20A` with a 5-row TTY and 20 lines).

comment.body:
I still see a resize regression. Render six lines in eight rows with `useCursor` at `y: 4`, then shrink to five rows. The cursor is on row 4, but `clear()` only moves up two rows, so the redraw pushes two stale lines into scollback. I tried calculating the erase from the previous height and capping the move at the new viewport. That fixed it. Could we share that calculation between the two shrink paths and add a test that checks which lines end up in scrollback? The final viewport looks right either way.

I’d use the existing home-and-erase sequence where we know the frame covers the top row. Clearing from the top unconditionally erased a shell line in my test with a shorter frame. There’s also a growth case where the clamp still misses. Render ten lines in five rows at `y: 7`, grow to ten rows, then call `clear()`. Both branches ask to move up seven rows from row 2. I’d leave that case for a follow-up and narrow the PR description accordingly.

issue.title: `prefer-global-this` should allow window.matchMedia
issue.body:
prefer-global-this rule contains exceptions: specific browser usages of window are allowed (like window.innerWidth)

window.matchMedia should also be allowed, it's a browser specific function not supported in Node.js

comment.body:
The exceptions are not based on whether an API exists in Node.js. Theyre for APIs where window is semantically meaningful, like window.innerWidth or window.top.

In browsers, globalThis.matchMedia works exactly like window.matchMedia. Neither works in Node.js, so using window provides no benefit. The same reasoning applies to the other APIs you listed.

If you need to guard browser-only code, use typeof window !== 'undefined', which the rule already allows.

awesome.md.content:
# The awesome manifesto

If you want your list to be included in `awesome`, try to only include actual awesome stuff in your list. After all, it's a curation, not a collection.

But **what is awesome?**

## Only awesome is awesome

Research if the stuff you're including is actually awesome. Only put stuff on the list that you or another contributor can personally recommend. You should rather leave stuff out than include too much.

## Awesome badge

This badge is for Awesome lists.

[![Awesome](https://awesome.re/badge.svg)](https://awesome.re)
[![Awesome](https://awesome.re/badge-flat.svg)](https://awesome.re)
[![Awesome](https://awesome.re/badge-flat2.svg)](https://awesome.re)

Add an awesome badge to the top of your list, right next to the title. [Example](https://github.com/sindresorhus/awesome-nodejs). You can choose either the regular badge or the flat one.

```md
[![Awesome](https://awesome.re/badge.svg)](https://awesome.re)
[![Awesome](https://awesome.re/badge-flat.svg)](https://awesome.re)
[![Awesome](https://awesome.re/badge-flat2.svg)](https://awesome.re)
```

You are allowed to use the badge on lists not included here and also on private lists.

*The badges should not be modified in any way.*

## Awesome mentioned badge

This badge is intended for projects featured in an Awesome list (**not for Awesome lists themselves**). For example, the [Chalk](https://github.com/chalk/chalk) project could feature this badge because it's listed in [Awesome Node.js](https://github.com/sindresorhus/awesome-nodejs). It's totally optional for projects, but it's a nice way to show they've been featured in an Awesome list. You can choose either the regular badge or the flat one.

[![Mentioned in Awesome](https://awesome.re/mentioned-badge.svg)](https://awesome.re)
[![Mentioned in Awesome](https://awesome.re/mentioned-badge-flat.svg)](https://awesome.re)

**Fill in the placeholders (Name and URL):**

```md
[![Mentioned in Awesome <INSERT LIST NAME>](https://awesome.re/mentioned-badge.svg)](https://github.com/<INSERT LIST URL>)
[![Mentioned in Awesome <INSERT LIST NAME>](https://awesome.re/mentioned-badge-flat.svg)](https://github.com/<INSERT LIST URL>)
```

Example:

```md
[![Mentioned in Awesome Node.js](https://awesome.re/mentioned-badge.svg)](https://github.com/sindresorhus/awesome-nodejs)
```

If you're an Awesome list maintainer, you could encourage projects in your list to add the badge.

*The badges should not be modified in any way.*

## Comment on why something is awesome

Apart from suggesting a particular item on your list, you should also inform your readers *why* it's on the list and how they will benefit from it.

## Make it clear what the list is about

Have a succinct description at the top of your readme. Make sure your list covers a certain scope and nothing else. Link to other awesome lists if you think they already cover a certain subject well enough.

## Pay attention to grammar

Ensure your list is grammatically correct, typo-free and has no Markdown formatting errors. This should also apply to pull requests.

## Choose an appropriate license

Keep in mind that if you [haven't selected a license](https://choosealicense.com/no-license/), it basically means the people are *not* allowed to reproduce, distribute or create derivative works.

[Creative Commons licenses](https://creativecommons.org/) are perfect for this purpose. **We would recommend [`CC0`](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/).** Code licenses like MIT, BSD, GPL, and so forth are not recommended.

## Include contribution guidelines

People who are contributing to your list should have a clear understanding of how they should do so.

If you don't feel like writing one from scratch, feel free to take our [contributing.md](contributing.md) and modify it to your own needs.

## Stylize your list properly

Create a [table of contents](https://github.com/sindresorhus/stuff/blob/main/toc-generators.md), organize the content into different categories, and use images if suitable. Ensure all entries are consistent (e.g. all entry descriptions end in a `.`).

## Accept other people's opinion

If you're an owner of the list, respect other people's opinions. If there are plenty of users not agreeing with your decision, give it a second thought.

# Contributor Covenant Code of Conduct

## Our Pledge

In the interest of fostering an open and welcoming environment, we as
contributors and maintainers pledge to making participation in our project and
our community a harassment-free experience for everyone, regardless of age, body
size, disability, ethnicity, gender identity and expression, level of experience,
nationality, personal appearance, race, religion, or sexual identity and
orientation.

## Our Standards

Examples of behavior that contributes to creating a positive environment
include:

* Using welcoming and inclusive language
* Being respectful of differing viewpoints and experiences
* Gracefully accepting constructive criticism
* Focusing on what is best for the community
* Showing empathy towards other community members

Examples of unacceptable behavior by participants include:

* The use of sexualized language or imagery and unwelcome sexual attention or
advances
* Trolling, insulting/derogatory comments, and personal or political attacks
* Public or private harassment
* Publishing others' private information, such as physical or electronic
  address, without explicit permission
* Other conduct that could reasonably be considered inappropriate in a
  professional setting

## Our Responsibilities

Project maintainers are responsible for clarifying the standards of acceptable
behavior and are expected to take appropriate and fair corrective action in
response to any instances of unacceptable behavior.

Project maintainers have the right and responsibility to remove, edit, or
reject comments, commits, code, wiki edits, issues, and other contributions
that are not aligned to this Code of Conduct, or to ban temporarily or
permanently any contributor for other behaviors that they deem inappropriate,
threatening, offensive, or harmful.

## Scope

This Code of Conduct applies both within project spaces and in public spaces
when an individual is representing the project or its community. Examples of
representing a project or community include using an official project e-mail
address, posting via an official social media account, or acting as an appointed
representative at an online or offline event. Representation of a project may be
further defined and clarified by project maintainers.

## Enforcement

Instances of abusive, harassing, or otherwise unacceptable behavior may be
reported by contacting the project team at sindresorhus@gmail.com. All

contributing.md.content:
# Contribution Guidelines

Please note that this project is released with a [Contributor Code of Conduct](code-of-conduct.md). By participating in this project you agree to abide by its terms.

## Adding an awesome list

Please ensure your pull request adheres to the [list of guidelines](pull_request_template.md).

## Creating your own awesome list

To create your own list, check out the [instructions](create-list.md).

## Adding something to an awesome list

If you have something awesome to contribute to an awesome list, this is how you do it.

You will need a [GitHub account](https://github.com/join)! If you are new to GitHub, [get started here](https://github.com/firstcontributions/first-contributions).

1. Access the awesome list's GitHub page. For example: https://github.com/sindresorhus/awesome
2. Click on the `readme.md` file: ![Step 2 Click on Readme.md](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/170270/9402920/53a7e3ea-480c-11e5-9d81-aecf64be55eb.png)
3. Now click on the edit icon. ![Step 3 - Click on Edit](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/170270/9402927/6506af22-480c-11e5-8c18-7ea823530099.png)
4. You can start editing the text of the file in the in-browser editor. Make sure you follow the guidelines above. You can use [GitHub Flavored Markdown](https://help.github.com/articles/github-flavored-markdown/). ![Step 4 - Edit the file](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/170270/9402932/7301c3a0-480c-11e5-81f5-7e343b71674f.png)
5. Say why you're proposing the changes, and then click on "Propose file change". ![Step 5 - Propose Changes](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/170270/9402937/7dd0652a-480c-11e5-9138-bd14244593d5.png)
6. Submit the [pull request](https://help.github.com/articles/using-pull-requests/)!

## Updating your Pull Request

Sometimes, a maintainer of an awesome list will ask you to edit your Pull Request before it is included. This is normally due to spelling errors or because your PR didn't match the awesome-* list guidelines.

[Here](https://github.com/RichardLitt/knowledge/blob/master/github/amending-a-commit-guide.md) is a write up on how to change a Pull Request and the different ways you can do that.

create-list.md.content:
# Creating Your Own List

- Read the [Awesome manifesto](awesome.md) and [list guidelines](pull_request_template.md) and ensure your list complies.
- Search this list before making a new one, as yours may be a duplicate. If it is, try and contribute to the best one instead of making your own.
- **Wait at least 30 days after creating a list before submitting it, to give it a chance to mature.**
- **Make sure you read the [list guidelines](pull_request_template.md) again before submitting a pull request for your list to be added here.**

Thanks for being awesome! 😎

pull_request_template.md.content:
**[Insert URL to the list here]** **[Explain what this list is about and why it should be included here]** ### By submitting this pull request I confirm I've read and complied with the below requirements 🖖 **Please read it multiple times. I spent a lot of time on these guidelines and most people miss a lot.** ## Requirements for your pull request - [ ] Fully AI-generated pull requests are not accepted. - [ ] Don't open a Draft / WIP pull request while you work on the guidelines. A pull request should be 100% ready and should adhere to all the guidelines when you open it. **Instead use [#2242](https://github.com/sindresorhus/awesome/issues/2242) for incubation visibility**. - [ ] **Don't waste my time.** Do a good job, adhere to all the guidelines, and be responsive. - [ ] **You have to review at least 4 other [open pull requests](https://github.com/sindresorhus/awesome/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen).** Try to prioritize unreviewed PRs, but you can also add more comments to reviewed PRs. Go through the below list when reviewing. This requirement is meant to help make the Awesome project self-sustaining. Comment here which PRs you reviewed. You're expected to put a good effort into this and to be thorough. Look at previous PR reviews for inspiration. **Just commenting “looks good” or simply marking the pull request as approved does not count!** You have to actually point out mistakes or improvement suggestions. Comments pointing out lint violation are allowed, but does **not** count as a review. - [ ] You have read and understood the [instructions for creating a list](https://github.com/sindresorhus/awesome/blob/main/create-list.md). - [ ] This pull request has a title in the format `Add Name of List`. It should not contain the word `Awesome`. - ✅ `Add Swift` - ✅ `Add Software Architecture` - ❌ `Update readme.md` - ❌ `Add Awesome Swift` - ❌ `Add swift` - ❌ `add Swift` - ❌ `Adding Swift` - ❌ `Added Swift` - [ ] Your entry here should include a short description of the project/theme of the list. **It should not describe the list itself.** The first character should be uppercase and the description should end in a dot. It should be an objective description and not a tagline or marketing blurb. It should not contain the name of the list. - ✅ `- [iOS](…) - Mobile operating system for Apple phones and tablets.` - ✅ `- [Framer](…) - Prototyping interactive UI designs.` - ❌ `- [iOS](…) - Resources and tools for iOS development.` - ❌ `- [Framer](…)` - ❌ `- [Framer](…) - prototyping interactive UI designs` - [ ] Your entry should be added at the bottom of the appropriate category. - [ ] The title of your entry should be title-cased and the URL to your list should end in `#readme`. - Example: `- [Software Architecture](https://github.com/simskij/awesome-software-architecture#readme) - The discipline of designing and building software.` - [ ] No blockchain-related lists. - [ ] The suggested Awesome list complies with the below requirements. ## Requirements for your Awesome list - [ ] **Has been around for at least 30 days.**
That means 30 days from either the first real commit or when it was open-sourced. Whatever is most recent. - [ ] Is not AI-generated. - [ ] Run [`awesome-lint`](https://github.com/sindresorhus/awesome-lint) on your list and fix the reported issues. If there are false-positives or things that cannot/shouldn't be fixed, please [report it](https://github.com/sindresorhus/awesome-lint/issues/new). - [ ] The default branch should be named [`main`, not `master`](https://www.zdnet.com/article/github-to-replace-master-with-alternative-term-to-avoid-slavery-references/). - [ ] **Includes a succinct description of the project/theme at the top of the readme.** [(Example)](https://github.com/willempienaar/awesome-quantified-self) - ✅ `Mobile operating system for Apple phones and tablets.` - ✅ `Prototyping interactive UI designs.` - ❌ `Resources and tools for iOS development.` - ❌ `Awesome Framer packages and tools.` - [ ] It's the result of hard work and the best I could possibly produce. **If you have not put in considerable effort into your list, your pull request will be immediately closed.** - [ ] The repo name of your list should be in lowercase slug format: `awesome-name-of-list`. - ✅ `awesome-swift` - ✅ `awesome-web-typography` - ❌ `awesome-Swift` - ❌ `AwesomeWebTypography` - [ ] The heading title of your list should be in [title case](https://capitalizemytitle.com/) format: `# Awesome Name of List`. - ✅ `# Awesome Swift` - ✅ `# Awesome Web Typography` - ❌ `# awesome-swift` - ❌ `# AwesomeSwift` - [ ] Non-generated Markdown file in a GitHub repo. - [ ] The repo should have `awesome-list` & `awesome` as [GitHub topics](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/managing-your-repositorys-settings-and-features/customizing-your-repository/classifying-your-repository-with-topics). I encourage you to add more relevant topics. - [ ] Not a duplicate. Please search for existing submissions. - [ ] Only has awesome items. Awesome lists are curations of the best, not everything. - [ ] Does not contain items that are unmaintained, has archived repo, deprecated, or missing docs. If you really need to include such items, they should be in a separate Markdown file. - [ ] Includes a project logo/illustration whenever possible. - Either centered, fullwidth, or placed at the top-right of the readme. [(Example)](https://github.com/sindresorhus/awesome-electron) - The image should link to the project website or any relevant website. - **The image should be high-DPI.** Set it to a maximum of half the width of the original image. - Don't include both a title saying `Awesome X` and a logo with `Awesome X`. You can put the header image in a `#` (Markdown header) or `

`. - [ ] Entries have a description, unless the title is descriptive enough by itself. It rarely is though. - [ ] Includes the [Awesome badge](https://github.com/sindresorhus/awesome/blob/main/awesome.md#awesome-badge). - Should be placed on the right side of the readme heading. - Can be placed centered if the list has a centered graphics header. - Should link back to this list. - [ ] Has a Table of Contents section. - Should be named `Contents`, not `Table of Contents`. - Should be the first section in the list. - Should only have one level of [nested lists](https://commonmark.org/help/tutorial/10-nestedLists.html), preferably none. - Must not feature `Contributing` or `Footnotes` sections. - [ ] Has an appropriate license. - **We strongly recommend the [CC0 license](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/), but any [Creative Commons license](https://creativecommons.org/choose/) will work.** - Tip: You can quickly add it to your repo by going to this URL: `https://github.com///community/license/new?branch=main&template=cc0-1.0` (replace `` and `` accordingly). - A code license like MIT, BSD, Apache, GPL, etc, is not acceptable. Neither are WTFPL and [Unlicense](https://unlicense.org). - Place a file named `license` or `LICENSE` in the repo root with the license text. - **Do not** add the license name, text, or a `Licence` section to the readme. GitHub already shows the license name and link to the full text at the top of the repo. - To verify that you've read all the guidelines, please comment on your pull request with just the word `unicorn`. - [ ] Has [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/sindresorhus/awesome/blob/main/awesome.md#include-contribution-guidelines). - The file should be named `contributing.md`. The casing is up to you. - It can optionally be linked from the readme in a dedicated section titled `Contributing`, positioned at the top or bottom of the main content. - The section should not appear in the Table of Contents. - [ ] All non-important but necessary content (like extra copyright notices, hyperlinks to sources, pointers to expansive content, etc) should be grouped in a `Footnotes` section at the bottom of the readme. The section should not be present in the Table of Contents. - [ ] Has consistent formatting and proper spelling/grammar. - The link and description are separated by a dash.
Example: `- [AVA](…) - JavaScript test runner.` - The description starts with an uppercase character and ends with a period. - Consistent and correct naming. For example, `Node.js`, not `NodeJS` or `node.js`. - [ ] Does not use [hard-wrapping](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/319925/difference-between-hard-wrap-and-soft-wrap). - [ ] Does not include a CI (e.g. GitHub Actions) badge.
You can still use a CI for linting, but the badge has no value in the readme. - [ ] Does not include an `Inspired by awesome-foo` or `Inspired by the Awesome project` kinda link at the top of the readme. The Awesome badge is enough. **Go to the top and read it again.**

4395.body:
The `<details>` / `<summary>` wrappers around every category are the biggest thing here. Each section is collapsed by default, so nothing is scannable without clicking through twelve of them, and it does not match the plain bullet-list structure Awesome lists use. I'd unfold them all.

The readme opens with "A quality-first, human-reviewed collection of web tools, apps, and resources for runners." That describes the list rather than the theme, which is the pattern the guidelines call out ("Resources and tools for iOS development" is their example of what to avoid). The line you used in the PR entry, "Recreational and competitive distance running", is much closer to what they want.

Two star solicitations should go: "Useful? Star this repository to find it again" near the top, and "please star the repo and share it with fellow runners" at the bottom. The PRs-welcome shields badge too.

Smaller things: the H1 is an image with no text, so there is no plain `# Awesome Running Tools` heading anywhere. And a few descriptions restate themselves, like WeatherToRun described as a "running condition advisor that helps determine optimal running conditions."

Took a look at awesome-running-tools. The `<details>` wrappers and star requests from the earlier review are gone, nice. A few things that haven't come up yet:

- Strava appears four times as separate entries: Strava Route Builder (Training and Planning), Strava (Performance Tracking), Strava App (Mobile Apps) and Strava Clubs (Motivation and Community). It's one product; a single entry covering routes, tracking and clubs would do.
- Some categories overlap. "Mobile Apps" is a platform rather than a use, so Nike Run Club and Couch to 5K sit apart from the tracking and training-plan tools they're alternatives to. "Training and Planning" and "Education and Training Plans" also overlap: DialPace's pace calculators are in one, the VDOT and McMillan calculators in the other.
- "Community" in Contents is a closing paragraph, not a list section, and the "Contributing" section at the bottom carries the submission template and checklist, which would fit better in CONTRIBUTING.md.
- A few entries are a store or a single organizer rather than a tool: Clever Training is a shop, and Spartan Race and NYRR are one organization's event sites. Next to Race Roster and RunSignUp they read as padding for a list that says it's quality-first.
- Calendar Hack's description ("Quick calendar tool for date calculations and viewing") doesn't say how it helps runners.

Hey @reinaldosimoes

I had a look at the list. The `<details>` and the star requests are gone, nice. I found some other things:

- WeatherToRun is the first entry and also the example in the README template and in CONTRIBUTING.md. The site has `<meta name="author" content="Reinaldo Simoes">` and links to reinaldo.pt, which is the website on your GitHub profile. Your CONTRIBUTING.md says no entries from people who own the tool, so I think you should disclose it or remove it and use another example.
- README lines 5-8 are hard-wrapped (4 lines that render as one paragraph).
- The banner links to the repo itself. The guidelines say the image should link to the project website or something relevant.
- Some links are old: `runsmartproject.com/calculator/` redirects to `vdoto2.com/calculator/`, `strava.com/routes/new` redirects to `/maps/create` and `strava.com/clubs` goes to the login page if you are not logged in.
- The descriptions are mixed. Some are like "Analyze your runs...", "Shop for...", "Join running clubs...", others are just nouns (Strava, parkrun). I would use one style, without "your".
- I'm not sure "Health and Social Science" is the right category, it is mostly research lists. Maybe Miscellaneous fits better?

The points from the previous review are still open (last push is from 08-30): Strava is there 4 times, "Community" in Contents is only a paragraph, the template/checklist should be in CONTRIBUTING.md, Clever Training is a shop and Spartan Race/NYRR are single organisers, the Calendar Hack description is not about running and some categories overlap.

Took a look. Couple of things I didn't see in the thread yet:

- contributing / code of conduct lines right under the title, these normally go down to a Contributing section
- Nutrition and Hydration has only one entry, Weather and Gear only two. Maybe merge with other sections

btw thanks for the license catch on mine back in august

Thanks @levz0r, @VascoSch92, and @sbarkalov. I addressed the new review points in [67e4e88](https://github.com/reinaldosimoes/awesome-running-tools/commit/67e4e88):

- Removed WeatherToRun from the list and contribution example to eliminate the affiliation conflict.
- Consolidated four Strava entries into one entry covering tracking, routes, and clubs.
- Reorganized eleven overlapping or undersized categories into six functional categories; mobile apps, calculators, weather, nutrition, gear, and gamification now sit with their use cases.
- Removed Calendar Hack, Clever Training, NYRR, and Spartan Race.
- Updated the VDOT calculator to its current name and URL.
- Removed Community from Contents and moved the README template/checklist into CONTRIBUTING.md.
- Moved contribution and Code of Conduct messaging to the bottom, changed the banner target to a neutral long-distance running reference, and standardized descriptions.

The list now has 29 entries. awesome-lint passes, all Contents links render, and the fresh GitHub link-health run completed with zero errors or timeouts.

Guideline review:

**Compliant:** `#readme` URL, sensible Health-section placement, description is objective and short.

**Concrete issue — name mismatch:** the entry reads `Running` but the repo is `awesome-running-tools`. The guidelines expect the entry name to match the list's actual name/topic; as written, a reader landing on "Running" gets a tools-specific list (watches, pacing apps, training logs, …), not a general running list. Either rename the entry to `Running Tools` or rename the repo to `awesome-running` and broaden the scope. This mismatch is the kind of thing that stalls otherwise clean PRs here.

**Minor:** the description "Recreational and competitive distance running." describes the sport, not the list's contents — one clause on what is actually curated (tools? communities? research?) would fix it.

Thanks @kevincouton. Fixed both points:

- Renamed the upstream entry and PR from `Running` to `Running Tools` so they match `awesome-running-tools` and the “Awesome Running Tools” heading.
- Expanded the description to “Training, performance tracking, route planning, race discovery, and communities for recreational and competitive distance running.” so the curated scope is explicit.

The index change is in [703a98d](https://github.com/reinaldosimoes/awesome/commit/703a98d), and the list’s matching description is in [d034cdd](https://github.com/reinaldosimoes/awesome-running-tools/commit/d034cdd). Both the list’s `awesome-lint` check and the upstream repository linter pass.

@CastelDazur @levz0r @VascoSch92 @sbarkalov @kevincouton Thank you for reviewing this submission. The changes in response to your feedback are published, with summaries in [the curation update](https://github.com/sindresorhus/awesome/pull/4395#issuecomment-6035661361) and [the naming and scope update](https://github.com/sindresorhus/awesome/pull/4395#issuecomment-6070288146). The banner remains an image H1, as permitted by the submission guidelines.

Could you please recheck the current list and submit a formal approval through GitHub's review interface if you are satisfied? If anything still needs work, please let me know. Both the list and upstream lint checks pass. Thanks again for your time.

4396.body:
I want to make an AI agent on my site also
Can I?

The readme's one-line description is "The most comprehensive open-source library of AI agent components." The guidelines ask for an objective description of the theme rather than a tagline, and "most comprehensive" is a claim, not a description. Worth rewriting to say what the list actually covers.

Second, the scope is very broad. Skills, MCPs, Agent Loops, Subagents, Hooks, Plugins, Prompts and Tools are eight fairly different artifact types sitting in one list. Together they read closer to "things that plug into AI coding assistants" than one coherent theme.

Last one: "What Makes This Different" and the Star History section are about the repo itself rather than the tools in it. I'd cut both and let the entries carry the list.

# Visual Studio Code - Open Source ("Code - OSS") [![Feature Requests](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/microsoft/vscode/feature-request.svg)](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Aissue+label%3Afeature-request+sort%3Areactions-%2B1-desc) [![Bugs](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/microsoft/vscode/bug.svg)](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues?utf8=✓&q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3Abug) ## The Repository This repository ("`Code - OSS`") is where we (Microsoft) develop the [Visual Studio Code](https://code.visualstudio.com) product together with the community. Not only do we work on code and issues here, but we also publish our [roadmap](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Roadmap), [monthly iteration plans](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Iteration-Plans), and our [endgame plans](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Running-the-Endgame). This source code is available to everyone under the standard [MIT license](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/LICENSE.txt). ## Visual Studio Code

[Visual Studio Code](https://code.visualstudio.com) is a distribution of the `Code - OSS` repository with Microsoft-specific customizations released under a traditional [Microsoft product license](https://code.visualstudio.com/License/). [Visual Studio Code](https://code.visualstudio.com) combines the simplicity of a code editor with what developers need for their core edit-build-debug cycle. It provides comprehensive code editing, navigation, and understanding support along with lightweight debugging, a rich extensibility model, and lightweight integration with existing tools. Visual Studio Code is updated monthly with new features and bug fixes. You can download it for Windows, macOS, and Linux on the [Visual Studio Code website](https://code.visualstudio.com/Download). To get the latest releases every day, install the [Insiders build](https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders). ## Contributing There are many ways in which you can participate in this project, for example: * [Submit bugs and feature requests](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues), and help us verify them as they are checked in * Review [source code changes](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pulls) * Review the [documentation](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-docs) and make pull requests for anything from typos to new content. If you are interested in fixing issues and contributing directly to the codebase, please see the document [How to Contribute](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute), which covers the following: * [How to build and run from source](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute) * [The development workflow, including debugging and running tests](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#debugging) * [Coding guidelines](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Coding-Guidelines) * [Submitting pull requests](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests) * [Finding an issue to work on](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#where-to-contribute) * [Contributing to translations](https://aka.ms/vscodeloc) ## Feedback * Ask a question on [Stack Overflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/vscode) * [Request a new feature](CONTRIBUTING.md) * Upvote [popular feature requests](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Aissue+label%3Afeature-request+sort%3Areactions-%2B1-desc) * [File an issue](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues) * Connect with the extension author community on [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-discussions/discussions) or [Slack](https://aka.ms/vscode-dev-community) * Follow [@code](https://x.com/code) and let us know what you think! See our [wiki](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Feedback-Channels) for a description of each of these channels and information on some other available community-driven channels. ## Related Projects Many of the core components and extensions to VS Code live in their own repositories on GitHub. For example, the [node debug adapter](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-node-debug) and the [mono debug adapter](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-mono-debug) repositories are separate from each other. For a complete list, please visit the [Related Projects](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Related-Projects) page on our [wiki](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki). ## Bundled Extensions VS Code includes a set of built-in extensions located in the [extensions](extensions) folder, including grammars and snippets for many languages. Extensions that provide rich language support (inline suggestions, Go to Definition) for a language have the suffix `language-features`. For example, the `json` extension provides coloring for `JSON` and the `json-language-features` extension provides rich language support for `JSON`. ## Development Container This repository includes a Visual Studio Code Dev Containers / GitHub Codespaces development container. * For [Dev Containers](https://aka.ms/vscode-remote/download/containers), use the **Dev Containers: Clone Repository in Container Volume...** command, which creates a Docker volume for better disk I/O on macOS and Windows. * If you already have VS Code and Docker installed, you can also click [here](https://vscode.dev/redirect?url=vscode://ms-vscode-remote.remote-containers/cloneInVolume?url=https://github.com/microsoft/vscode) to get started. This will cause VS Code to automatically install the Dev Containers extension if needed, clone the source code into a container volume, and spin up a dev container for use. * For Codespaces, install the [GitHub Codespaces](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=GitHub.codespaces) extension in VS Code, and use the **Codespaces: Create New Codespace** command. Docker / the Codespace should have at least **4 cores and 6 GB of RAM (8 GB recommended)** to run a full build. See the [development container README](.devcontainer/README.md) for more information. ## Code of Conduct This project has adopted the [Microsoft Open Source Code of Conduct](https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/). For more information, see the [Code of Conduct FAQ](https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/faq/) or contact [opencode@microsoft.com](mailto:opencode@microsoft.com) with any additional questions or comments. ## License Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation. Canvas: fix pill and restore canvas after worktree session switch in the editor window (#349496)

* Fix canvas pill not revealing its canvas in the editor window

The sessions-UI pill builds its canvas owner from the session model, while the editor window only knows owners from the chat model's canvasContext. The owners never matched, so revealCanvas returned silently. Resolve the requested owner to the visible widget's canonical owner before revealing.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* canvases: keep a canvas that a folder location working-set swap closed while its owner was hidden

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* canvases: keep a canvas through a working-set swap while its owner is visible

Applying the folder location working set closes the canvas editors of a window without working sets of its own. That close was taken for a dismissal, so the canvas did not show again on its owner.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* canvases: infer working-set suspension only from an actual apply

sessions: Let agents create Dev Containers and continue work in them (#349231)

* sessions: Let agents create Dev Containers and continue work in them

Adds the create_dev_container tool, which creates a Dev Container environment through the same path as the Remote Environments create action and returns its host and workspace for create_remote_session, and the built-in dev-container-handoff skill that guides the handoff. Both are behind chat.agentHost.devContainer.handoff.enabled, which also enables the remote session tools and requires Dev Container environments.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: Add a smoke test for continuing work in a Dev Container

A scripted agent creates a Dev Container environment with create_dev_container and starts a session in it with create_remote_session. Environment containers have no workspace devcontainer.json, so smoke tests pass the settings that point their Agent Host at the mock server in VSCODE_SMOKE_TEST_DEV_CONTAINER_ENVIRONMENT_CONFIG. The automation also accepts the 'Allow in this Session' confirmation of Agent Host client tools.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: Name Dev Container environment volumes like New Dev Container

New environments get a volume and workspace folder named like the Dev Containers extension's New Dev Container names them: ubuntu, then ubuntu-2 and so on when the name is taken on the Docker host. The host finds an environment's volumes by its label instead of deriving their names from its identifier, so a volume created concurrently under the same name moves on to the next one, and removal deletes every volume labeled with the environment, including its state volume.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: Link the Create Dev Container tool's progress to the container's log

createEnvironment reports the new environment before its container starts, so the tool's progress message, and its result message, open the environment's Dev Container log, like the session preparation of a workspace's Dev Container. The smoke test opens the log through the link and warms up the Agent Host first, so the session it scripts starts after the remote session tools are registered.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: label the folder Dev Container environment 'Dev Container for Folder'

Distinguishes the environment that runs the selected folder in the Dev Container it configures from the standalone Dev Containers listed in the picker.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: create Dev Containers on the invoking session's host by default

create_dev_container without a host now uses the host that the invoking session runs on, or for a session in a Dev Container environment the host that runs that container, and falls back to this computer when that host cannot run Dev Containers. Previously a session on a WSL, SSH, or Tunnel host created the container on this computer.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: wait until a new Dev Container can start sessions

create_dev_container now waits for the same host checks that create_remote_session applies, exposed as IRemoteSessionService.getHostRejections, and returns a notReady result with the reasons and recovery guidance when the container cannot start sessions in time. Without a requested host, it no longer picks the only remote host when Docker is unavailable on this computer and the session does not run there.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: keep the approved host and clean up legacy state volumes of Dev Container environments

create_dev_container now creates the container only on the host that the user approved, and resolves sessions in a folder's Dev Container to the host of the folder. Removing an environment also removes a state volume that was created before state volumes were labeled with their environment. The Dev Container handoff smoke test installs a CLI in the container, since the update server has none for the commit of an unpublished build.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: isolate Dev Container environment state and smoke test cleanup

A new environment no longer takes a workspace name whose state volume exists, and an environment never mounts a state volume labeled with another environment. create_dev_container can request pre-approval, so calls from a background chat wait for a chat to confirm them. The handoff smoke test labels its containers and only removes the environments with that label.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: bind the approved Dev Container host to the chat and call

Agents choose tool call IDs, so the host approved in create_dev_container's confirmation is now kept per originating chat and call ID. An invocation without a known approved host creates nothing.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* smoke: accept a Dev Container environment's log before the Dev Containers CLI writes to it

The handoff suite opens the environment's log while its container is still being created; on CI the base image pull can keep the Dev Containers CLI from logging for longer than the wait.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Model picker: list all of a required agent's models without folding (#349274)

An agent with model-policy: required already narrows the picker to the
models it allows. The Copilot tab still curated that list into a
shortlist and folded the rest behind a collapsed Other Models toggle,
so one of the agent's models needed an expand and a scroll to reach.

🤖 Authored with GitHub Copilot on behalf of @aeschli.

sessions: preserve acknowledgement and Inbox focus (#349498)

Keep existing Inbox triage decisions when opening a session resolves timing within its known modified time. Preserve wake-up on newer activity and notifications.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: keep focus and selection in Inbox after acknowledgement

Restore the list's position after toolbar and context-menu acknowledgement without switching the active conversation. Preserve unrelated selected rows.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Experiment: offer 'open in Markdown Editor' in the classic empty editor hint (#349457)

* Offer 'open in Markdown Editor' in the classic empty editor hint (experimental)

Adds workbench.editor.experimental.emptyEditorHintOpenInMarkdownEditor (off, onExp). When on, the one-line hint of a new untitled file that the Markdown Editor can open also offers to reopen it there, like the Open in row of the list of actions. The emptyEditorHint telemetry logs it as variant classicMarkdownEditor and the click as openMarkdownEditor. The reopen logic of the list moves to a shared EmptyEditorHintReopener.

Fixes #349455

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Move the empty editor hint registrations into emptyTextEditorHint.contribution.ts

So that tests can import the hint classes without registering the editor contribution and the Escape keybinding.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Remove comments that restate the code in the empty editor hint

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Empty editor hint: move classes to emptyTextEditorHintController.ts

emptyTextEditorHint.ts registers the contribution and keybindings again, as on main, so no new *.contribution.ts enters the mobile import graph (check-mobile-boundary). Importers that need the classes use the registration-free controller module.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

chat: show hook files the Copilot harness won't run (#349334)

* chat: show hook files the Copilot harness won't run

VS Code's Local harness runs hook files from places the Copilot harness does
not read, such as folders added with chat.hookFilesLocations, so those hooks
silently stopped running in Copilot sessions.

Chat Customizations now lists these files with a "Won't run" badge that tells
the user to move the file to .github/hooks or ~/.copilot/hooks and check that
its scripts work with Copilot. They are found by comparing the Local harness's
hook files with the ones the agent host reports, so VS Code keeps no copy of
the runtime's rules. This is done only for the local Copilot agent host, once
its hook discovery has loaded, and leaves out Claude Code hook files. For a
worktree session, files of the workspace folder belong to its repository;
configured folders outside the workspace are included. The list refreshes
when hook files change.

Fixes #342668

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

issues.title: editor: respect screen-reader mode for Agents Markdown defaults
issues.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Summary

Make `workbench.editor.markdownDefaultEditorInAgentsWindow` screen-reader-aware, following the existing automatic accessibility-setting pattern:

- `auto` (default): use the Markdown editor normally and the text editor in screen-reader mode.
- `on`: always prefer the Markdown editor.
- `off`: retain the existing Markdown Preview fallback.

Update both Markdown file and diff defaults when screen-reader mode changes, without reopening existing editors or overriding explicit editor associations. Migrate stored boolean preferences from `true` to `on` and `false` to `off`, and add localized mode descriptions and the accessibility tag. Retain compatibility with legacy boolean default assignments.

## Validation

- `pnpm run gulp compile-client` — passed, zero compilation errors.
- `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --run src/vs/workbench/services/editor/test/browser/editorResolverService.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/test/browser/parts/editor/editorConfiguration.test.ts` — passed, 40 tests.
- `./scripts/test.sh --isolate --reporter dot --run src/vs/workbench/services/editor/test/browser/editorResolverService.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/test/browser/parts/editor/editorConfiguration.test.ts` — both files passed independently.
- `pnpm run oxlint src/vs/workbench/services/editor/common/editorResolverService.ts src/vs/workbench/browser/parts/editor/editorConfiguration.ts src/vs/workbench/services/editor/test/browser/editorResolverService.test.ts src/vs/workbench/test/browser/parts/editor/editorConfiguration.test.ts` — passed.
- `pnpm run valid-layers-check` — passed.
- `pnpm run check-cyclic-dependencies` — passed.

Tests cover all three modes with screen-reader mode on/off, live updates, boolean migration/default compatibility, HTML defaults, and explicit user/workspace associations.

## Manual Testing

In the Agents window, leave the setting at `auto` and toggle `editor.accessibilitySupport` between `on` and `off`. Open fresh Markdown files and diffs after each change: expect the text editor with screen-reader mode on and the Markdown editor with it off. Verify that `on` always prefers the Markdown editor, `off` prefers Markdown Preview, and explicit editor associations remain respected.

Live VoiceOver testing and full integration/smoke suites were not run.

issues.title: ci: allow cold setup in the WebKit job timeout
issues.body:
## Why

The merge-queue [Linux / Browser-Unit (WebKit) job](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/44797139897/job/136499707615) exceeded its 12-minute whole-job timeout. Cold setup took about five minutes, and only three of four test workers completed before cancellation. PR Gate then failed with `linux-tests did not succeed (result: cancelled)`, removing #344732 from the queue. Another [WebKit job](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/44800514415/job/136511305773) exhausted the same budget while installing WebKit, before tests started.

## Change

Increase only `browser-unit-webkit.timeout-minutes` in `.github/workflows/pr-linux-test.yml` from **12 to 35 minutes**. Budget approximately 15 minutes for cold setup (including the existing 10-minute WebKit installation allowance), the existing 15-minute test-step allowance, and five minutes of headroom for setup variability and cleanup. Replace the outdated comment that tied the timeout to a roughly 13-minute merge-queue target.

The WebKit installation step remains limited to 10 minutes and the test step to 15 minutes. Runners, test selection, retries, gating and all other jobs are unchanged. This raises the worst-case queue wait; it does not resolve genuine test failures or guarantee that every cold setup succeeds. Installation optimization and diagnostics are deliberately out of scope. The existing #349239 optimizes package installation but does not increase this job timeout, so this is a separate focused change.

## Validation

- Parsed the before/after workflow using the repository's existing `js-yaml` dependency, including its shared steps anchor.
- Asserted the job timeout changes from 12 to 35 and the WebKit test/install step timeouts remain 15/10.
- Deep-compared the parsed workflows after normalizing that one timeout: no other semantic changes.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- No CI reruns were requested. The WebKit job is merge-queue-only, so normal PR checks do not validate its full runtime behavior.

## Signing

This PR contains an unsigned commit and is **awaiting owner signing**. It is intentionally a draft; no merge or deployment was requested.

> Authored with Copilot

issues.title: New tab button: second press on + opens the tab in the button's group
issues.body:
Fixes #349526

With `workbench.editor.newTabButton` on, pressing the new tab (+) button opens its menu, and pressing + again while the menu is open picks the default entry. Every entry opens its tab in the editor group of the + that was pressed, but the second press opened it in the active group instead: with the left group focused, pressing + twice in the right group put the new chat editor (or untitled file) into the left group. Picking the same entry from the menu worked.

The second press ran the entry with `toolbar.context`, but `ToolBar` only has a setter for `context`, so it read `undefined`. The entry then fell back to the active group. It now runs with the context the control was created with, as the menu does.

Validation:
- The existing second-press test of the new tab button now also checks that each pick, including the second press, runs with the group of its button.
- In Code OSS with two groups and the left one focused, pressing + twice in the right group now opens the chat editor and the untitled file in the right group. Before the fix both opened in the left group.

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

issues.body:
With `workbench.editor.newTabButton` on, the new tab (+) button at the end of the editor tabs opens its menu on the first press, and a second press on + picks the default entry (the entry picked last, see #348560).

Each entry should open its tab in the editor group of the + that was pressed. Picking an entry from the menu does that, but picking it with the second press on + opens it in the active editor group instead.

Steps:
1. Enable `workbench.editor.newTabButton`.
2. Split the editor into two groups and focus an editor in the left group.
3. Press + in the right group, then press + again.

Expected: the new tab opens in the right group.
Actual: it opens in the left (focused) group. This happens for every entry, e.g. New Chat Editor and New Untitled Text File.

issues.title: sessions: batch group archives with bounded concurrency
issues.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Addresses #349504.

## Summary

Mark All as Done previously awaited each comparison participant before starting the next. Large groups therefore paid the subscription and host-confirmation delay for every session sequentially.

- Add provider-neutral bulk archiving with bounded concurrency and an optional provider batch operation.
- Limit Agent Host archives to four concurrent operations per provider and merge their session-change notifications.
- Preserve active-request cancellation, authoritative host confirmation, rejection handling, and comparison-group restoration through Undo.
- Wait for every outcome before reporting failures or offering Undo. An unsuccessful session does not prevent independent sessions from completing, and every successful archive remains undoable.

This PR deliberately retains the existing confirmed protocol path. Avoiding cold-session restoration requires a separate confirmation-delivery change; it is not replaced with fire-and-forget dispatch. Worktree cleanup remains host-owned and backgrounded.

## Validation

- `pnpm run compile-client` — passed, including client type checking.
- `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --run src/vs/sessions/services/sessions/test/browser/sessionsManagementService.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsArchiveActions.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/test/browser/localAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsSessionManagementActions.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsList.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/services/sessions/test/browser/sessionNavigation.test.ts` — passed: 1,845 tests; 13 existing pending.
- `pnpm run build-fast --client-only && ./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/test/browser/localAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts --grep 'bulk archive|archive waits for host confirmation'` — passed: 3 tests after adding the timing assertion. The 90-session batch uses at most four concurrent confirmations and completes in 230 ms of simulated time with 10 ms per archive, including one rejection.
- `pnpm run oxlint src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/browser/sessionsManagementService.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/browser/views/sessionsListActions.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/providers/agentHost/browser/baseAgentHostSessionsProvider.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/common/sessionsManagement.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/common/sessionsProvider.ts src/vs/sessions/services/sessions/test/browser/sessionNavigation.test.ts src/vs/sessions/services/sessions/test/browser/sessionsManagementService.test.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsArchiveActions.test.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsListTestUtils.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/test/browser/localAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts` — passed.
- `pnpm run valid-layers-check` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

Live-provider UI timing, cross-platform smoke tests, and cold-session end-to-end timings were not exercised.

## Manual testing

1. Create a custom group containing multiple completed comparisons, totaling approximately 90 participant sessions.
2. Invoke Mark All as Done and confirm. Verify multiple participants are processed concurrently and the completed comparison groups retire.
3. Invoke Undo. Verify successful sessions and their comparison-group membership are restored.
4. Repeat with a disconnected or rejected participant. Verify errors are reported and all successful archives remain undoable.

issues.title: Report Markdown constructs in Markdown Editor sessions
issues.body:
Fixes #349520

To find out what keeps people from using the Markdown Editor, we want to compare revert and retention rates by the Markdown constructs their documents use: maybe documents with HTML blocks or footnotes are where the editor falls short. This PR adds flags for those constructs to the existing `markdownEditor.session` event (from https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/348911):

`hasMermaid`, `hasMath`, `hasHtmlBlock`, `hasFrontMatter`, `hasTable`, `hasFootnote`, `hasTaskList` (`true`/`false`) and `headingCountBucket` (`0`, `1-5`, `6-20`, `>20`). No content is reported.

## Performance

Opening the Markdown Editor must not get slower, so the scan is kept off the open path and bounded:

- It runs once per session, **2 seconds after the editor opened**, not while opening. It is cancelled if the editor closes before that; such sessions report no flags.
- Documents of **100k characters or more are not scanned** (they report no flags).
- It is **one pass over the lines with simple, anchored regular expressions**, no markdown-it parse.

Measured with Node (median of 50 runs, documents just under 100k characters):

| Document | ms per scan |
| --- | --- |
| realistic mixed Markdown | 0.8 |
| one 99k-character line | 0.1 |
| many `$` signs | 1.0 |
| table-like lines | 3.5 |
| 33k tiny fenced blocks (worst case) | 8.5 |

The table separator regex was also checked for catastrophic backtracking on single lines up to 98k characters: time grows linearly (6 ms at 98k). A unit test fails if scanning a 100k-character document takes more than 20 ms.

Being a line-based heuristic, it skips fenced code but not, for example, indented code blocks. Inline `$...$` math follows the usual dollar-math rule (no space inside, no digit after the closing `$`), so prices like "$5 and $10" do not count.

## Validation

- Unit tests for the scan (constructs inside fenced code are ignored, prices are not math) and for the session event.
- Code OSS with trace logging: a document with front matter, a Mermaid block, a table and inline math open for 4 s reports exactly those flags; a document closed after 0.5 s reports no flags.
- Markdown extension typecheck and integration tests (221 passing).

issues.title: Report who reaches the Markdown Editor nudge (markdownEditor.nudgeContext)
issues.body:
Fixes #349519

The Markdown Editor nudges (https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/349251) are about to be compared in an experiment (control, text editor nudge, preview nudge). To learn *which* Markdown users keep the Markdown Editor, the results need to be split by the kind of user: someone with extensions that extend the Markdown preview, or with another Markdown editor installed, may react very differently from someone who only writes plain Markdown.

This PR adds one event, `markdownEditor.nudgeContext`, sent once per profile at the moment a nudge would show. It is sent in every experiment arm, including control (where no spotlight is shown), so all arms are segmented the same way. To time it, the onboarding service gets an `onDidReachWouldShow` event, fired right after it opens the experiment's assignment-context gate; the context event is logged from there, so it always carries the arm.

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `nudge` | `textEditor` or `preview`: the situation that reached the nudge |
| `previewExtensionCount` | enabled non-built-in extensions with an active `markdown.markdownItPlugins`, `markdown.previewScripts` or `markdown.previewStyles` contribution (same rules as the Markdown extension) |
| `otherMarkdownEditorCount` | editors for Markdown files other than the text editor, the Markdown Editor and the Markdown Preview (editors registered for every file, `*`, are not counted) |
| `defaultBefore` | `text`, `markdownPreview` or `other` |
| `editedMarkdownRecently` | a Markdown file was edited in the last 7 days |
| `untitledMarkdownEditorUsed` | the empty editor hint last opened an untitled file in the Markdown Editor |

Only counts and flags are reported, no extension ids. Being a core event, it carries the experiment assignment context.

`editedMarkdownRecently` uses a new profile timestamp of the last Markdown edit, written at most once per hour, so it only knows about edits after this version is installed.

## Validation

- Unit tests for the counting helpers (built-in and inactive preview contributions are excluded, editors for `*` are not counted), and the onboarding control-arm test asserts the assignment id already flows when `onDidReachWouldShow` fires.
- Code OSS, fresh profile, control arm simulated with `experiments.override.onb.markdownEditorNudge.*` (`show: false`, id `onb-mdnudge-control`): after the startup grace, opening `planning.md`, `notes.md` and `planning.md` again logs exactly one `markdownEditor.nudgeContext` (`nudge: textEditor`, `defaultBefore: text`, all counts 0) and shows no spotlight.
- Core typecheck, oxlint, layer check.

### Description
VS Code adds `<install-dir>\bin\copilot-shim` (`vscode-copilot-launcher`) to Windows `PATH`, exposing a `copilot` shim executable globally even when GitHub Copilot CLI is not installed.

When tools (such as CLI session/agent managers like Herdr) or environments inheriting Windows `PATH` (such as WSL) check `PATH` for `copilot`, they detect the launcher shim as an available CLI and trigger an interactive install prompt (`Install GitHub Copilot CLI? [y/N]`) when invoked.

### Expected Behavior
- Provide a setting, installer task/flag (compatible with `winget` / Inno Setup), or policy option to opt out of adding `bin\copilot-shim` to `PATH` (or disable the `copilot` shim launcher) while keeping `code` on `PATH`.

### Actual Behavior
- `which copilot` (from WSL) or `Get-Command copilot` resolves to `...\Microsoft VS Code\bin\copilot-shim\copilot` even when Copilot CLI is not installed, causing `PATH`-based tool detection to treat `copilot` as present.

### Environment
- OS: Windows (with WSL)
- VS Code: 1.146 (installed via WinGet `Microsoft.VisualStudioCode`)
- Copilot CLI: Not installed

pulls.body:

## Summary

Make `workbench.editor.markdownDefaultEditorInAgentsWindow` screen-reader-aware, following the existing automatic accessibility-setting pattern:

- `auto` (default): use the Markdown editor normally and the text editor in screen-reader mode.
- `on`: always prefer the Markdown editor.
- `off`: retain the existing Markdown Preview fallback.

Update both Markdown file and diff defaults when screen-reader mode changes, without reopening existing editors or overriding explicit editor associations. Migrate stored boolean preferences from `true` to `on` and `false` to `off`, and add localized mode descriptions and the accessibility tag. Retain compatibility with legacy boolean default assignments.

pulls.title: ci: allow cold setup in the WebKit job timeout
pulls.body:
## Why

The merge-queue [Linux / Browser-Unit (WebKit) job](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/44797139897/job/136499707615) exceeded its 12-minute whole-job timeout. Cold setup took about five minutes, and only three of four test workers completed before cancellation. PR Gate then failed with `linux-tests did not succeed (result: cancelled)`, removing #344732 from the queue. Another [WebKit job](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/44800514415/job/136511305773) exhausted the same budget while installing WebKit, before tests started.

## Change

Increase only `browser-unit-webkit.timeout-minutes` in `.github/workflows/pr-linux-test.yml` from **12 to 35 minutes**. Budget approximately 15 minutes for cold setup (including the existing 10-minute WebKit installation allowance), the existing 15-minute test-step allowance, and five minutes of headroom for setup variability and cleanup. Replace the outdated comment that tied the timeout to a roughly 13-minute merge-queue target.

The WebKit installation step remains limited to 10 minutes and the test step to 15 minutes. Runners, test selection, retries, gating and all other jobs are unchanged. This raises the worst-case queue wait; it does not resolve genuine test failures or guarantee that every cold setup succeeds. Installation optimization and diagnostics are deliberately out of scope. The existing #349239 optimizes package installation but does not increase this job timeout, so this is a separate focused change.

## Validation

- Parsed the before/after workflow using the repository's existing `js-yaml` dependency, including its shared steps anchor.
- Asserted the job timeout changes from 12 to 35 and the WebKit test/install step timeouts remain 15/10.
- Deep-compared the parsed workflows after normalizing that one timeout: no other semantic changes.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- No CI reruns were requested. The WebKit job is merge-queue-only, so normal PR checks do not validate its full runtime behavior.

## Signing

This PR contains an unsigned commit and is **awaiting owner signing**. It is intentionally a draft; no merge or deployment was requested.

> Authored with Copilot

The second press ran the entry with `toolbar.context`, but `ToolBar` only has a setter for `context`, so it read `undefined`. The entry then fell back to the active group. It now runs with the context the control was created with, as the menu does.

Validation:
- The existing second-press test of the new tab button now also checks that each pick, including the second press, runs with the group of its button.
- In Code OSS with two groups and the left one focused, pressing + twice in the right group now opens the chat editor and the untitled file in the right group. Before the fix both opened in the left group.
