pulls.title: sessions: batch group archives with bounded concurrency
pulls.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Addresses #349504.

## Summary

Mark All as Done previously awaited each comparison participant before starting the next. Large groups therefore paid the subscription and host-confirmation delay for every session sequentially.

- Add provider-neutral bulk archiving with bounded concurrency and an optional provider batch operation.
- Limit Agent Host archives to four concurrent operations per provider and merge their session-change notifications.
- Preserve active-request cancellation, authoritative host confirmation, rejection handling, and comparison-group restoration through Undo.
- Wait for every outcome before reporting failures or offering Undo. An unsuccessful session does not prevent independent sessions from completing, and every successful archive remains undoable.

This PR deliberately retains the existing confirmed protocol path. Avoiding cold-session restoration requires a separate confirmation-delivery change; it is not replaced with fire-and-forget dispatch. Worktree cleanup remains host-owned and backgrounded.

## Validation

- `pnpm run compile-client` — passed, including client type checking.
- `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --run src/vs/sessions/services/sessions/test/browser/sessionsManagementService.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsArchiveActions.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/test/browser/localAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsSessionManagementActions.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsList.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/services/sessions/test/browser/sessionNavigation.test.ts` — passed: 1,845 tests; 13 existing pending.
- `pnpm run build-fast --client-only && ./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/test/browser/localAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts --grep 'bulk archive|archive waits for host confirmation'` — passed: 3 tests after adding the timing assertion. The 90-session batch uses at most four concurrent confirmations and completes in 230 ms of simulated time with 10 ms per archive, including one rejection.
- `pnpm run oxlint src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/browser/sessionsManagementService.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/browser/views/sessionsListActions.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/providers/agentHost/browser/baseAgentHostSessionsProvider.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/common/sessionsManagement.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/common/sessionsProvider.ts src/vs/sessions/services/sessions/test/browser/sessionNavigation.test.ts src/vs/sessions/services/sessions/test/browser/sessionsManagementService.test.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsArchiveActions.test.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsListTestUtils.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/test/browser/localAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts` — passed.
- `pnpm run valid-layers-check` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

Live-provider UI timing, cross-platform smoke tests, and cold-session end-to-end timings were not exercised.

## Manual testing

1. Create a custom group containing multiple completed comparisons, totaling approximately 90 participant sessions.
2. Invoke Mark All as Done and confirm. Verify multiple participants are processed concurrently and the completed comparison groups retire.
3. Invoke Undo. Verify successful sessions and their comparison-group membership are restored.
4. Repeat with a disconnected or rejected participant. Verify errors are reported and all successful archives remain undoable.

pulls.title: Report Markdown constructs in Markdown Editor sessions
pulls.body:
Fixes #349520

To find out what keeps people from using the Markdown Editor, we want to compare revert and retention rates by the Markdown constructs their documents use: maybe documents with HTML blocks or footnotes are where the editor falls short. This PR adds flags for those constructs to the existing `markdownEditor.session` event (from https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/348911):

`hasMermaid`, `hasMath`, `hasHtmlBlock`, `hasFrontMatter`, `hasTable`, `hasFootnote`, `hasTaskList` (`true`/`false`) and `headingCountBucket` (`0`, `1-5`, `6-20`, `>20`). No content is reported.

## Performance

Opening the Markdown Editor must not get slower, so the scan is kept off the open path and bounded:

- It runs once per session, **2 seconds after the editor opened**, not while opening. It is cancelled if the editor closes before that; such sessions report no flags.
- Documents of **100k characters or more are not scanned** (they report no flags).
- It is **one pass over the lines with simple, anchored regular expressions**, no markdown-it parse.

Measured with Node (median of 50 runs, documents just under 100k characters):

| Document | ms per scan |
| --- | --- |
| realistic mixed Markdown | 0.8 |
| one 99k-character line | 0.1 |
| many `$` signs | 1.0 |
| table-like lines | 3.5 |
| 33k tiny fenced blocks (worst case) | 8.5 |

The table separator regex was also checked for catastrophic backtracking on single lines up to 98k characters: time grows linearly (6 ms at 98k). A unit test fails if scanning a 100k-character document takes more than 20 ms.

Being a line-based heuristic, it skips fenced code but not, for example, indented code blocks. Inline `$...$` math follows the usual dollar-math rule (no space inside, no digit after the closing `$`), so prices like "$5 and $10" do not count.

## Validation

- Unit tests for the scan (constructs inside fenced code are ignored, prices are not math) and for the session event.
- Code OSS with trace logging: a document with front matter, a Mermaid block, a table and inline math open for 4 s reports exactly those flags; a document closed after 0.5 s reports no flags.
- Markdown extension typecheck and integration tests (221 passing).

pulls.title: Report who reaches the Markdown Editor nudge (markdownEditor.nudgeContext)
pulls.body:
Fixes #349519

The Markdown Editor nudges (https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/349251) are about to be compared in an experiment (control, text editor nudge, preview nudge). To learn *which* Markdown users keep the Markdown Editor, the results need to be split by the kind of user: someone with extensions that extend the Markdown preview, or with another Markdown editor installed, may react very differently from someone who only writes plain Markdown.

This PR adds one event, `markdownEditor.nudgeContext`, sent once per profile at the moment a nudge would show. It is sent in every experiment arm, including control (where no spotlight is shown), so all arms are segmented the same way. To time it, the onboarding service gets an `onDidReachWouldShow` event, fired right after it opens the experiment's assignment-context gate; the context event is logged from there, so it always carries the arm.

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `nudge` | `textEditor` or `preview`: the situation that reached the nudge |
| `previewExtensionCount` | enabled non-built-in extensions with an active `markdown.markdownItPlugins`, `markdown.previewScripts` or `markdown.previewStyles` contribution (same rules as the Markdown extension) |
| `otherMarkdownEditorCount` | editors for Markdown files other than the text editor, the Markdown Editor and the Markdown Preview (editors registered for every file, `*`, are not counted) |
| `defaultBefore` | `text`, `markdownPreview` or `other` |
| `editedMarkdownRecently` | a Markdown file was edited in the last 7 days |
| `untitledMarkdownEditorUsed` | the empty editor hint last opened an untitled file in the Markdown Editor |

Only counts and flags are reported, no extension ids. Being a core event, it carries the experiment assignment context.

`editedMarkdownRecently` uses a new profile timestamp of the last Markdown edit, written at most once per hour, so it only knows about edits after this version is installed.

## Validation

- Unit tests for the counting helpers (built-in and inactive preview contributions are excluded, editors for `*` are not counted), and the onboarding control-arm test asserts the assignment id already flows when `onDidReachWouldShow` fires.
- Code OSS, fresh profile, control arm simulated with `experiments.override.onb.markdownEditorNudge.*` (`show: false`, id `onb-mdnudge-control`): after the startup grace, opening `planning.md`, `notes.md` and `planning.md` again logs exactly one `markdownEditor.nudgeContext` (`nudge: textEditor`, `defaultBefore: text`, all counts 0) and shows no spotlight.
- Core typecheck, oxlint, layer check.

CONTRIBUTING.md.content:
# Contributing to VS Code

Welcome, and thank you for your interest in contributing to VS Code!

There are several ways in which you can contribute, beyond writing code. The goal of this document is to provide a high-level overview of how you can get involved.

## Asking Questions


Have a question? Instead of opening an issue, please ask on [Stack Overflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/visual-studio-code) using the tag `visual-studio-code`.

The active community will be eager to assist you. Your well-worded question will serve as a resource to others searching for help.

## Providing Feedback

Your comments and feedback are welcome, and the development team is available via a handful of different channels.

See the [Feedback Channels](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Feedback-Channels) wiki page for details on how to share your thoughts.

## Reporting Issues

Have you identified a reproducible problem in VS Code? Do you have a feature request? We want to hear about it! Here's how you can report your issue as effectively as possible.

### Identify Where to Report

The VS Code project is distributed across multiple repositories. Try to file the issue against the correct repository. Check the list of [Related Projects](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Related-Projects) if you aren't sure which repo is correct.

Can you recreate the issue even after [disabling all extensions](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/editor/extension-gallery#_disable-an-extension)? If you find the issue is caused by an extension you have installed, please file an issue on the extension's repo directly.

### Look For an Existing Issue

Before you create a new issue, please do a search in [open issues](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues) to see if the issue or feature request has already been filed.

Be sure to scan through the [most popular](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Aissue+label%3Afeature-request+sort%3Areactions-%2B1-desc) feature requests.

If you find your issue already exists, make relevant comments and add your [reaction](https://github.com/blog/2119-add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments). Use a reaction in place of a "+1" comment:

* 👍 - upvote
* 👎 - downvote

If you cannot find an existing issue that describes your bug or feature, create a new issue using the guidelines below.

### Writing Good Bug Reports and Feature Requests

File a single issue per problem and feature request. Do not enumerate multiple bugs or feature requests in the same issue.

Do not add your issue as a comment to an existing issue unless it's for the identical issue. Many issues look similar but have different causes.

The more information you can provide, the more likely someone will be successful at reproducing the issue and finding a fix.

The built-in tool for reporting an issue, which you can access by using `Report Issue` in VS Code's Help menu, can help streamline this process by automatically providing the version of VS Code, all your installed extensions, and your system info. Additionally, the tool will search among existing issues to see if a similar issue already exists.

Please include the following with each issue:

* Version of VS Code
* Your operating system
* List of extensions that you have installed
* Reproducible steps (1... 2... 3...) that cause the issue
* What you expected to see, versus what you actually saw
* Images, animations, or a link to a video showing the issue occurring
* A code snippet that demonstrates the issue or a link to a code repository the developers can easily pull down to recreate the issue locally
  * **Note:** Because the developers need to copy and paste the code snippet, including a code snippet as a media file (i.e. .gif) is not sufficient.
* Errors from the Dev Tools Console (open from the menu: Help > Toggle Developer Tools)

### Creating Pull Requests

* Please refer to the article on [creating pull requests](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests) and contributing to this project.

### Final Checklist

Please remember to do the following:

* [ ] Search the issue repository to ensure your report is a new issue
* [ ] Recreate the issue after disabling all extensions
* [ ] Simplify your code around the issue to better isolate the problem

Don't feel bad if the developers can't reproduce the issue right away. They will simply ask for more information!

### Follow Your Issue

Once submitted, your report will go into the [issue tracking](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Issue-Tracking) workflow. Be sure to understand what will happen next, so you know what to expect and how to continue to assist throughout the process.

## Automated Issue Management

We use GitHub Actions to help us manage issues. These Actions and their descriptions can be [viewed here](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-github-triage-actions). Some examples of what these Actions do are:

* Automatically close any issue marked `info-needed` if there has been no response in the past 7 days.
* Automatically lock issues 45 days after they are closed.
* Automatically implement the VS Code [feature request pipeline](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Issues-Triaging#managing-feature-requests).

If you believe the bot got something wrong, please open a new issue and let us know.

## Contributing Fixes

If you are interested in writing code to fix issues, please see [How to Contribute](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute) in the wiki.

This repository installs its dependencies with [pnpm](https://pnpm.io). Install pnpm 11 or newer (for example `npm install -g pnpm`), then run `pnpm install` at the repository root. pnpm commands in the repository run with the pnpm version that the `packageManager` field of [package.json](package.json) pins: pnpm downloads that version the first time and switches to it. Installing with npm or yarn is not supported.

## Thank You

Your contributions to open source, large or small, make great projects like this possible. Thank you for taking the time to contribute.

README.md.content:
# Visual Studio Code - Open Source ("Code - OSS") [![Feature Requests](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/microsoft/vscode/feature-request.svg)](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Aissue+label%3Afeature-request+sort%3Areactions-%2B1-desc) [![Bugs](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/microsoft/vscode/bug.svg)](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues?utf8=✓&q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3Abug) ## The Repository This repository ("`Code - OSS`") is where we (Microsoft) develop the [Visual Studio Code](https://code.visualstudio.com) product together with the community. Not only do we work on code and issues here, but we also publish our [roadmap](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Roadmap), [monthly iteration plans](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Iteration-Plans), and our [endgame plans](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Running-the-Endgame). This source code is available to everyone under the standard [MIT license](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/LICENSE.txt). ## Visual Studio Code

[Visual Studio Code](https://code.visualstudio.com) is a distribution of the `Code - OSS` repository with Microsoft-specific customizations released under a traditional [Microsoft product license](https://code.visualstudio.com/License/). [Visual Studio Code](https://code.visualstudio.com) combines the simplicity of a code editor with what developers need for their core edit-build-debug cycle. It provides comprehensive code editing, navigation, and understanding support along with lightweight debugging, a rich extensibility model, and lightweight integration with existing tools. Visual Studio Code is updated monthly with new features and bug fixes. You can download it for Windows, macOS, and Linux on the [Visual Studio Code website](https://code.visualstudio.com/Download). To get the latest releases every day, install the [Insiders build](https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders). ## Contributing There are many ways in which you can participate in this project, for example: * [Submit bugs and feature requests](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues), and help us verify them as they are checked in * Review [source code changes](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pulls) * Review the [documentation](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-docs) and make pull requests for anything from typos to new content. If you are interested in fixing issues and contributing directly to the codebase, please see the document [How to Contribute](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute), which covers the following: * [How to build and run from source](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute) * [The development workflow, including debugging and running tests](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#debugging) * [Coding guidelines](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Coding-Guidelines) * [Submitting pull requests](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests) * [Finding an issue to work on](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#where-to-contribute) * [Contributing to translations](https://aka.ms/vscodeloc) ## Feedback * Ask a question on [Stack Overflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/vscode) * [Request a new feature](CONTRIBUTING.md) * Upvote [popular feature requests](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Aissue+label%3Afeature-request+sort%3Areactions-%2B1-desc) * [File an issue](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues) * Connect with the extension author community on [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-discussions/discussions) or [Slack](https://aka.ms/vscode-dev-community) * Follow [@code](https://x.com/code) and let us know what you think! See our [wiki](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Feedback-Channels) for a description of each of these channels and information on some other available community-driven channels. ## Related Projects Many of the core components and extensions to VS Code live in their own repositories on GitHub. For example, the [node debug adapter](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-node-debug) and the [mono debug adapter](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-mono-debug) repositories are separate from each other. For a complete list, please visit the [Related Projects](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Related-Projects) page on our [wiki](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki). ## Bundled Extensions VS Code includes a set of built-in extensions located in the [extensions](extensions) folder, including grammars and snippets for many languages. Extensions that provide rich language support (inline suggestions, Go to Definition) for a language have the suffix `language-features`. For example, the `json` extension provides coloring for `JSON` and the `json-language-features` extension provides rich language support for `JSON`. ## Development Container This repository includes a Visual Studio Code Dev Containers / GitHub Codespaces development container. * For [Dev Containers](https://aka.ms/vscode-remote/download/containers), use the **Dev Containers: Clone Repository in Container Volume...** command, which creates a Docker volume for better disk I/O on macOS and Windows. * If you already have VS Code and Docker installed, you can also click [here](https://vscode.dev/redirect?url=vscode://ms-vscode-remote.remote-containers/cloneInVolume?url=https://github.com/microsoft/vscode) to get started. This will cause VS Code to automatically install the Dev Containers extension if needed, clone the source code into a container volume, and spin up a dev container for use. * For Codespaces, install the [GitHub Codespaces](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=GitHub.codespaces) extension in VS Code, and use the **Codespaces: Create New Codespace** command. Docker / the Codespace should have at least **4 cores and 6 GB of RAM (8 GB recommended)** to run a full build. See the [development container README](.devcontainer/README.md) for more information. ## Code of Conduct This project has adopted the [Microsoft Open Source Code of Conduct](https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/). For more information, see the [Code of Conduct FAQ](https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/faq/) or contact [opencode@microsoft.com](mailto:opencode@microsoft.com) with any additional questions or comments. ## License Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation. All rights reserved. Licensed under the [MIT](LICENSE.txt) license.

* Resolve types and imports of workspace members from the hoisted node_modules

With pnpm's hoisted workspace, a member's dependencies are usually in a parent
node_modules: extension tsconfigs look up their `types` like Node.js instead of
only in their own `node_modules/@types`, imports into an extension's own
node_modules use the package name, and undeclared imports that now resolve to
another member's version are declared or imported through their declared parent.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Cover pnpm lockfiles and pnpmfiles in the agent host test selection test

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* ci: install and run with pnpm in GitHub Actions

- Add a setup-pnpm composite action that installs the pnpm version pinned
  by `packageManager` (pnpm/action-setup v6.1.0, pinned by SHA) and use it
  in every workflow and action that installs dependencies or runs scripts.
- `npm ci` retry loops become `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`.
- The Copilot and component explorer jobs install only the root project
  with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts --filter .` (pnpm
  runs the root lifecycle scripts on every install, and they install every
  other install root), then the separate roots they need
  (`extensions/copilot`, `build`, `build/rspack`) with
  `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` in those folders.
- `npm run x -- args` becomes `pnpm run x args`: pnpm passes a literal `--`
  on to the script, also inside npm-run-all2 patterns.
- Run `build/npm/pnpm/verify-locks.ts` in the compile job while npm and
  pnpm lockfiles coexist.
- Read the telemetry extractor version from pnpm-lock.yaml.
- Watch pnpm-lock.yaml, pnpm-workspace.yaml and .pnpmfile.mts in the
  detect-changes and Agent Host E2E change detection.
- Point Dependabot at the pnpm workspace root for the Markdown editor.
- Switch the worktree build agent hook to pnpm.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* ci: install and run with pnpm in Azure Pipelines

- Add common/install-pnpm.yml, which installs the pnpm version pinned by
  `packageManager` with `npm install -g` from the configured registry
  (skipped when that version is already on PATH), and include it after the
  npm registry authentication of every job that uses pnpm. node_modules
  jobs only install it when their cache missed. The flaky smoke test jobs,
  which don't set up the registry themselves, use its setupRegistry option.
- `npm ci` retry loops become `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`; `npm run x
  -- args` becomes `pnpm run x args`, `npm run x --prefix d` becomes
  `pnpm -C d run x`, `npm exec --`/`npx` become `pnpm exec`.
- The Copilot pipelines install only the root project without its install
  scripts (`--ignore-scripts --filter .`), then the separate
  `extensions/copilot` root.
- The sanity tests install test/sanity with pnpm; their cache key uses its
  pnpm-lock.yaml, and the registry is configured on every run because pnpm
  itself comes from it.
- dependencies-check watches the pnpm files and installs every root with
  `pnpm_config_ignore_scripts`/`pnpm_config_frozen_lockfile=false`, so the
  clean git state check still reports outdated lockfiles. The removed
  check-allow-scripts step is covered by `strictDepBuilds` in every other
  install.
- The quality checks verify the pnpm lockfiles including the distro while
  npm and pnpm lockfiles coexist (non-blocking).
- Read the telemetry extractor version from pnpm-lock.yaml.
- Run build's own zx for Windows codesigning instead of an unpinned one
  that `npx` downloaded at run time.
- Drop npm-only settings (foreground scripts, timing logs).
- Keep npm where it is not about this repository's dependencies:
  vscode-capi (separate repository), the agent SDK tarballs, global tool
  installs and one-off published tools.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* build: use pnpm in scripts, editor tasks and the dev container

- scripts/*.sh|*.bat and the chat simulation scripts run `pnpm run`;
  `npm run x -- args` becomes `pnpm run x args` because pnpm passes a
  literal `--` on to the script.
- scripts/test.sh installs with `pnpm install` when node_modules is missing.
- xterm-update.js uses `pnpm view` and `pnpm add` with caret ranges (pnpm
  saves the exact version otherwise, npm saved `^version`).
- The npm tasks in .vscode/tasks.json become shell tasks running pnpm;
  "npm: install" dependencies use the Install Dependencies task.
- Workspace settings: npm.packageManager is pnpm, pnpm-lock.yaml is
  read-only. The Git unit test launch configuration uses the hoisted mocha.
- vscode-extras tells developers to run pnpm install.
- The dev container installs the pinned pnpm, keeps the pnpm store on the
  /vscode-dev volume and runs `pnpm install`.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* docs: use pnpm in contributor docs and agent instructions

- Repository commands in CONTRIBUTING files, READMEs, skills, instructions
  and agent docs use pnpm: `pnpm install`, `pnpm run x` (without `--`,
  which pnpm would pass on to the script), `pnpm -C dir run x`,
  `pnpm exec` for repository tools and `pnpm dlx` for one-off tools.
- CONTRIBUTING.md and copilot-instructions.md state that the repository
  installs with pnpm at the version that `packageManager` pins.
- Local package links use `link:` dependencies or `pnpm link <dir>`, which
  records an override in pnpm-workspace.yaml; `file:` directories are
  copies in pnpm.
- Keep npm where it is about something else: upstream repositories,
  published packages, the agent SDK packaging, global tools, user-project
  examples, changelogs and test fixtures. `npx @playwright/cli` keeps
  resolving the locally installed CLI and is part of skill tool patterns.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Use pnpm in the chat-lib package pipeline and the remaining editor tasks

- The chat-lib package pipelines (extensions/copilot/build/npm-package.yml
  and npm-package-next.yml, through steps/build-chat-lib.yml and
  test-chat-lib.yml) ran `npm ci` in extensions/copilot and chat-lib, which
  have no package-lock.json any more. They install the pinned pnpm after
  the npm registry setup and run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`,
  `pnpm run extract-chat-lib`, `pnpm run build` and `pnpm test`, like the
  GitHub test-chat-lib action. The template's own npm version, pack and
  publish steps are unchanged.
- The Copilot editor tasks install with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`
  and run `pnpm run`; its dev container installs the pinned pnpm before
  `pnpm install`.
- The html-language-features tasks ran `npm i compile` and `npm i watch`
  (from the yarn to npm switch, where `yarn compile` meant the script):
  they run `pnpm run compile` and `pnpm run watch`.
- The agent host coverage script and the codex protocol generator tell
  developers to run `pnpm install`.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Skip the workspace member links when listing node_modules for the CI caches

- pnpm links every workspace member into the root node_modules, including
  `vscode-extensions -> ../extensions`. listNodeModules.ts followed these
  links, so every node_modules cache archive (GitHub Actions and Azure
  Pipelines) stored the members' folders and every extension's
  node_modules a second time (macOS: 257,462 -> 176,577 files,
  7.1 -> 4.4 GiB).
- Directory links inside node_modules are skipped (lstat also reports
  Windows junctions as links); file links such as the .bin entries are
  listed as before. Nothing loads a workspace member through these links.
- Bump build/.cachesalt to drop the existing caches.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Lock chat-lib's changed dependencies to Copilot's versions without resolving

- The extraction copied Copilot's lockfile entries but left chat-lib's own
  dependency entries unchanged, so after a rollback within a compatible
  range (^3.2.0 -> ^3.1.0) the resolving install kept the newer version.
  It also resolved versions from the registry, also in the pipelines that
  publish chat-lib.
- copyLockedDependencies (chatLibLockfile.ts) locks each changed
  dependency to Copilot's specifier and version, replaces chat-lib's
  entries of its whole subtree with Copilot's (as the npm implementation
  did), drops removed dependencies and unused entries, and fails if an
  entry is missing.
- The extraction then runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --lockfile-only`,
  which only checks the result against chat-lib's package.json and pnpm's
  supply-chain policies, and writes it in pnpm's format.
- Tests for a rollback, an upgrade, an npm alias, a removal and missing
  entries.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Install the separate install roots frozen when the outer install is

- pnpm passes neither --frozen-lockfile nor its CI default to install
  scripts, so the `pnpm install` that the root postinstall runs in build,
  remote, extensions/copilot, ... updated their lockfiles also under
  `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` (which preLaunch.ts runs) and `pnpm ci`.
  The root .pnpmfile.mts runs in the pnpm process and exports the option
  from pnpm's command line as pnpm_config_frozen_lockfile, which the
  nested installs inherit; `pnpm ci` and its aliases count as
  --frozen-lockfile. CI keeps relying on pnpm's own default, and a plain
  `pnpm install` still updates the lockfiles.
- The install state hash includes build/npm/pnpm/nativeBuildEnv.ts, which
  every pnpmfile imports; a test checks every pnpmfile import.
- Fix the indentation of `git config pull.rebase merges`.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Keep the leading dot of dot-prefixed project folders in getLockfileFolder

`.vscode/extensions/vscode-extras` became `vscode/extensions/vscode-extras`
and was not recognized as a workspace member. Only a `./` prefix (or `.`
alone) is removed now.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Pass the native build settings to pnpm 12 from .mjs pnpmfiles

pnpm 12 loads only JavaScript pnpmfiles (.js, .mjs, .cjs): it fails on
.pnpmfile.mts with ERR_PNPM_PNPMFILE_NOT_FOUND. It also runs the
pnpmfile in a separate Node.js process, so the npm_config_* variables
that the pnpmfiles set on process.env never reached the install scripts.

Each native install root (the workspace, build, remote) now has a
.pnpmfile.mjs that exports createNativeBuildHooks() from
nativeBuildEnv.ts, so the code stays in TypeScript. Its updateConfig
hook returns the variables as extraEnv, which pnpm passes to every
dependency install script and lifecycle script. extraEnv can't remove a
variable, so a native build key that the root's .npmrc doesn't set gets
an empty value; node-gyp treats it like a missing one. The three files
are added to .eslint-allowed-javascript-files.

pnpm passes neither --frozen-lockfile nor its command line to the
pnpmfile or to scripts, only the command: `pnpm ci` and its aliases are
reported as npm_command `ci`. The root hook then sets
pnpm_config_frozen_lockfile for the installs of the separate install
roots. A local `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` can't be passed on, so
preLaunch.ts and update-all-grammars.ts also set
PNPM_CONFIG_FROZEN_LOCKFILE. In CI, pnpm's default freezes every install.

References to .pnpmfile.mts (install state hash, CI cache keys, change
detection, ripple, dependencies-check) now name .pnpmfile.mjs.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Pin pnpm 12.16.0 and adapt the conversion tooling and settings to pnpm 12

12.16.0 is the first pnpm 12 release with the fixes for a wrong peer
variant under the hoisted linker (pnpm/pnpm#17395) and for re-importing
patched packages on every install (pnpm/pnpm#17188).

Settings of every install root:
- pmOnFail: ignore. With a pinned packageManager, pnpm 12 records the
  pnpm packages of every platform in a second YAML document of
  pnpm-lock.yaml, which js-yaml's load, yaml.parse and GitHub's
  dependency graph can't read; a frozen install fails without it. ignore
  keeps the lockfiles single-document. pnpm then no longer switches
  another version to the pinned one; the preinstall's check names it.
- skills.dirs: []. pnpm 12 links the agent skills that approved
  dependencies ship into the skill folders of the coding agent it
  detects (.github/skills or .agents/skills here), and asks for
  approval on every install.
The setting names are checked against the pnpm 12.16.0 documentation.

Lockfiles: pnpm records pnpmfileChecksum for a pnpmfile with hooks. The
conversion generates lockfiles in a copy without the pnpmfile, so it
adds the checksum (SHA-256 of the pnpmfile with LF line endings, as
pnpm computes it) where pnpm writes it, and validates the result with
--ignore-pnpmfile. verify-locks checks the checksum (k) and fails on a
second YAML document (l).

getPnpmCommand also runs Corepack's native pnpm-native executable
directly, so nested installs started by `corepack pnpm` reuse it.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* List pnpm 12's links between project node_modules for the CI caches

pnpm 12's hoisted linker links a dependency to the same version in
another project's node_modules instead of copying it, for example
extensions/npm/node_modules/which to extensions/git/node_modules/which.
listNodeModules.ts skipped every directory link under node_modules, so
a restored cache resolved such a dependency to another version (for
extensions/npm, which@2.0.2 from the root instead of which@4.0.0).

A directory link whose target is inside a node_modules folder is now
listed; tar keeps it as a link, and its target is listed too. The
workspace member links in the root node_modules, whose targets are the
members' folders, are still skipped. build/.cachesalt is bumped.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Exempt each install root from the release-age check only for packages it installs

Every pnpm-workspace.yaml got the same minimumReleaseAgeExclude list, also install roots
that have none of those packages, such as build/npm/gyp with node-gyp only. Each root now
gets the patterns that match a package one of its projects installs, as with
allowBuilds and patchedDependencies, and no list when none match.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Pin the pnpm-capable distro

Pins microsoft/vscode-distro at ffdcd895811 (the merge of
microsoft/vscode-distro#1480), which adds pnpm-lock.yaml and
pnpm-workspace.yaml files next to the npm ones in npm/, npm/remote and
npm/remote/web. Its tree is identical to the PR head 4c7e27840cb that the
Azure product builds of this migration were validated with. The previous
pin, 165a83e58ea, is its first parent, so no distro change is rolled
back. release/1.145 keeps pinning the npm-only distro.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Generate pnpm lockfiles and workspace files from the npm lockfiles

Generated with `node build/npm/pnpm/convert.ts && node build/npm/pnpm/verify-locks.ts`
(pnpm 12.16.0) from the npm state of the parent commit. Drop and regenerate this commit
instead of editing it.

* sessions: split the Sessions part into a frame, a content registry and the session grid content

The Sessions part did two jobs: the frame (card, sizing, progress bar, visibility)
and the Agents window's session grid (slots of session views, drop target, chat
background, context keys). Split them so the frame can be shared:

- SessionsPart is the frame. Its window names the kind of content to show; the part
  looks the kind up in SessionsPartContentRegistry, creates the content in its
  constructor with its own instantiation service, renders and lays it out, and
  disposes it with itself. An unknown kind is a programming error and throws.
- SessionsPartContentRegistry is a plain registry object: defining it registers
  nothing. The Agents window registers its grid from
  vs/sessions/browser/parts/sessionsPartContent.registration.ts, loaded only by its
  entry point.
- SessionsGridContent is the former grid half of the part, moved verbatim. It binds
  the same context keys at the same moment, tracks focus on the same content area
  and asks the part to lay out again where the part used to re-run its last layout.
- SessionsParts passes the grid's id and delegates the grid API to the content;
  MobileSessionsPart lays out the content through the frame's layoutContent hook.

Tests and fixtures construct the part with the grid kind and use the content for
the grid API. New tests cover the registry, the selection of the named kind, the
creation scope, the render order, visibility, relayout and disposal.

No behavior change.

* Pass the native build settings to pnpm 12 from .mjs pnpmfiles

pnpm 12 loads only JavaScript pnpmfiles (.js, .mjs, .cjs): it fails on
.pnpmfile.mts with ERR_PNPM_PNPMFILE_NOT_FOUND. It also runs the
pnpmfile in a separate Node.js process, so the npm_config_* variables
that the pnpmfiles set on process.env never reached the install scripts.

Each native install root (the workspace, build, remote) now has a
.pnpmfile.mjs that exports createNativeBuildHooks() from
nativeBuildEnv.ts, so the code stays in TypeScript. Its updateConfig
hook returns the variables as extraEnv, which pnpm passes to every
dependency install script and lifecycle script. extraEnv can't remove a
variable, so a native build key that the root's .npmrc doesn't set gets
an empty value; node-gyp treats it like a missing one. The three files
are added to .eslint-allowed-javascript-files.

pnpm passes neither --frozen-lockfile nor its command line to the
pnpmfile or to scripts, only the command: `pnpm ci` and its aliases are
reported as npm_command `ci`. The root hook then sets
pnpm_config_frozen_lockfile for the installs of the separate install
roots. A local `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` can't be passed on, so
preLaunch.ts and update-all-grammars.ts also set
PNPM_CONFIG_FROZEN_LOCKFILE. In CI, pnpm's default freezes every install.

References to .pnpmfile.mts (install state hash, CI cache keys, change
detection, ripple, dependencies-check) now name .pnpmfile.mjs.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Pin pnpm 12.16.0 and adapt the conversion tooling and settings to pnpm 12

12.16.0 is the first pnpm 12 release with the fixes for a wrong peer
variant under the hoisted linker (pnpm/pnpm#17395) and for re-importing
patched packages on every install (pnpm/pnpm#17188).

Settings of every install root:
- pmOnFail: ignore. With a pinned packageManager, pnpm 12 records the
  pnpm packages of every platform in a second YAML document of
  pnpm-lock.yaml, which js-yaml's load, yaml.parse and GitHub's
  dependency graph can't read; a frozen install fails without it. ignore
  keeps the lockfiles single-document. pnpm then no longer switches
  another version to the pinned one; the preinstall's check names it.
- skills.dirs: []. pnpm 12 links the agent skills that approved
  dependencies ship into the skill folders of the coding agent it
  detects (.github/skills or .agents/skills here), and asks for
  approval on every install.
The setting names are checked against the pnpm 12.16.0 documentation.

Lockfiles: pnpm records pnpmfileChecksum for a pnpmfile with hooks. The
conversion generates lockfiles in a copy without the pnpmfile, so it
adds the checksum (SHA-256 of the pnpmfile with LF line endings, as
pnpm computes it) where pnpm writes it, and validates the result with
--ignore-pnpmfile. verify-locks checks the checksum (k) and fails on a
second YAML document (l).

getPnpmCommand also runs Corepack's native pnpm-native executable
directly, so nested installs started by `corepack pnpm` reuse it.

  the typed readers of the Electron and server Node.js versions; the
  preinstall, gulpfile.reh, darwin signing, useRunnerNodeForServer, the test
  launchers and the Alpine pipelines use them or the field.
- The node_modules cache key hashes the `nativeBuild` field; the Electron
  download cache key hashes build/checksums/electron.txt; change detection and
  ripple no longer list the `.npmrc` files.
- The shipped `package.json` files don't include the field.
